claims: Psychedelic drugs primarily work by affecting serotonin receptors in the brain.
Common types of psychedelic drugs include LSD, psilocybin ("magic mushrooms"), and DMT.
Effects of psychedelic drugs are highly dependent on the user's mindset ("set") and environment ("setting").
Common reactions to psychedelic drugs include dilated pupils.
Common reactions to psychedelic drugs include increased heart rate.
Common reactions to psychedelic drugs include sometimes nausea.
Classical psychedelics are generally not considered addictive.
LSD is lysergic acid diethylamide.
LSD is a synthetic compound derived from a fungus.
LSD is often taken on blotter paper.
Mescaline (Peyote) is derived from a cactus.
DMT is N,N-Dimethyltryptamine.
DMT is a potent, fast-acting compound found in various plants and animals.
Ayahuasca is a psychoactive brew containing DMT and other ingredients.
Emerging research indicates that substances like psilocybin and LSD have potential for treating depression, anxiety, and PTSD.
Psychedelic drugs are largely classified as Schedule 1 drugs in the U.S. and many other places.
Schedule 1 drugs are considered to have high abuse potential.
Schedule 1 drugs are considered to have no accepted medical use.
Ketamine is a dissociative compound.
PCP is phencyclidine.
PCP is a dissociative compound.
MDMA is ecstasy.
MDMA is an entactogen.
Psychedelic drugs are illegal in most jurisdictions.
